news.title: 2026 World Cup: Did Football Really Win?
news.lede: Years from now, football historians will remember the 2026 FIFA World Cup not only because Spain lifted the trophy, but because it was the tournament that rewrote football’s traditional hierarchy. Brazil’s elimination by Norway, Morocco proving once again that 2022 was no coincidence, Spain’s triumph through discipline rather than star power, and the controversies surrounding the final dominated headlines around the world. A World Cup has come to an end. But this time, it was not only one team that emerged victorious.

news.title: Gianni Infantino, Fifa and the week that rocked the football world
news.lede: Plan for sale of commercial rights to World Cup causes chaos with Uefa, AFC and Concacaf leading the opposition. It has been a week that has rocked football. The news caught everyone by surprise. When reports first emerged on Tuesday afternoon that Fifa, world football’s governing body, was to launch a vehicle to control the commercial rights to the World Cup, and would sell a stake of this company to investors, even members of the central decision-making body, the Fifa Council, hadn’t known about it.

news.title: Infantino under huge pressure after plan for World Cup sell-off sparks resignation and rebuke
news.lede: Cordeiro quits as senior adviser to Fifa president. Lamour: sell-off plan ‘defies belief and imagination’. The walls started closing in on Gianni Infantino after another dramatic day that saw one of his senior advisers resign and brought a scathing rebuke from Fifa’s own chief operating officer. Infantino is under huge pressure after his plan to sell chunks of the World Cup to private investors met a tide of opposition from around the globe.

news.title: FIFA wants to sell part of its World Cup business to Trump-linked investors. Global soccer is in revolt.
news.lede: The 2026 FIFA World Cup may have just ended, but the next one, it seems, is already mired in controversy. On Thursday, the 55 member associations of the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) — a group that includes perennial soccer powerhouses such as Spain, France, England and Germany — unanimously threatened to boycott all FIFA competitions going forward. FIFA is the governing body for international soccer and oversees the sport's major international competitions. That means if UEFA were to follow through, no European national teams would compete at the 2030 World Cup in Spain, Portugal and Morocco — or at next summer's Women's World Cup in Brazil.

news.title: United front against Infantino: AFC backs UEFA and CONCACAF in rejecting FIFA's World Cup sale plan.
news.lede: The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) aligned itself this Friday with UEFA and CONCACAF in rejecting the creation of FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), the project through which FIFA aims to open the commercial exploitation of competitions such as the World Cup to private investment. The Asian body called for an urgent review of the governance of the body chaired by Gianni Infantino in a statement, in which it expressed its "deep concern" and asserted that the initiative "cannot realistically achieve the broad consensus and unity needed to move forward," thus aligning itself with the positions previously defended by the European confederation and the North, Central America and Caribbean confederation. The Asian statement is another setback for FIFA, after UEFA warned of the consequences the initiative could have and CONCACAF denounced the lack of prior consultation.

news.title: Gianni Infantino: Why Africa might back Fifa's controversial World Cup plan
news.lede: Confederation of African Football president Patrice Motsepe (right) has developed a close working relationship with Fifa counterpart Gianni Infantino. In the row which has engulfed global football and the man who runs it, Gianni Infantino, could Africa end up as a lone voice of support for the Fifa president? While European governing body Uefa has voted to boycott Fifa competitions, including World Cups, if plans go ahead to sell stakes in those competitions to private investors, the Confederation of African Football (Caf) has remained largely silent so far. Much of that has to do with the close relationship between Caf, Fifa and Infantino.

news.title: Uefa has formed a rare but fragile united front against Fifa in battle for football’s future | Nick Ames and Matt Hughes
news.lede: Emerging from this week with unity over Fifa’s World Cup sell off was quite an acheivement but Europe cannot rest on its laurels. It was a phrase not always heard when Europe’s football associations discuss a pressing issue. “Touchingly unanimous,” was the assessment of a senior Uefa executive within moments of Thursday afternoon’s seismic decision to boycott Fifa tournaments unless Gianni Infantino scraps his private investment plan. United fronts on this scale are vanishingly rare and there is now a narrow window in which to make it count.

news.title: Senior FIFA executive says staff were deceived over Infantino's World Cup sell-off plan
news.lede: The new adidas Trionda Final ball, the official match ball for the semi-finals, the third-place play-off and final of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, on the pitch at Dallas Stadium, Arlington, Texas, on July 12, 2026. Photo by Leonardo Benassatto/Reuters. GENEVA (AP) — FIFA's chief operating officer said its staff were deceived by their president Gianni Infantino's World Cup sell-off plan, and suggested on Friday the project must not go ahead.
